metadata.note: The Newport and Sherman's Valley Railroad, a 3 ft gauge line built by lumberman David Gring from the Pennsylvania Railroad at Newport up Little Buffalo Creek and west through Sherman's Valley to Blain (1892) and New Germantown (1893), Perry County PA; 29.1 mi (Fowler). Sold with the Susquehanna River and Western on 31 Mar 1920 and absorbed into it; the Newport end closed in April 1920, and the SR&W ran the rest (Bloomfield Junction - New Germantown) until passenger service ended on 31 Dec 1928. Three features: N&SV Newport - Blain 1892-1920, N&SV Blain - New Germantown 1893-1920, SR&W Bloomfield Junction - New Germantown 1920-1928 (Rule 4 split at the 1920 sale; the SR&W feature shares the N&SV features' geometry). Research report: research/branches/newport_and_sherman_s_valley_railroad.txt.
sources: Kohler & Weinshencker, 'Narrow Gauge in the Sherman's Valley', as summarised in the chronology at https://pvrr.blogspot.com/2008/07/
John Fowler, Pennsylvania Railroads (5), tables 427 (N&SV) and 457 (SR&W); letter z = 1893 Official Guide: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/pennsylvaniarrs5.pdf
HMdb, Blain marker (Lions Club / Historical Society of Perry County, 2020), text read only via search-engine summaries: https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=257366
HMdb, 'The Railroad Era' marker, Newport, read via search summary only: https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=175062
pahistoricpreservation.com, 'From creek came village: Blain' (cites Gilmore, 'A Small Town Rich in History', 2017, pp. 77, 110): https://pahistoricpreservation.com/from-creek-came-village-blain/

OpenHistoricalMap (2026-10-21): dated railway=rail ways for the N&SV (1890-1935) and the Perry County RR
metadata.ownership_split: 31 Mar 1920 (sale to Rodney Gring and George H. Ross; absorbed into the SR&W) - chosen over the Blain marker's 1921. David Gring's 1903 purchase of the Perry County RR (reorganised as the SR&W) is NOT a split: the N&SV stayed a separate company running its own trains until 1920. USRA control 1917-18 is not a split.
omitted: New Bloomfield - Bloomfield Junction connection (1903 narrow-gauge rail, dual gauge 1918): drawable NONE in the report; the track belongs to the Perry County RR / SR&W standard-gauge layer, and no source says narrow-gauge passenger trains ran into New Bloomfield.
Path Valley extension beyond New Germantown (never completed) and the c.1901-1905 lumber railroad / Perry Lumber Company railroad on its roadbed: freight/logging only (Rule 1).
Perry County RR Landisburg extension via Elliottsburg and Green Park (OHM 1892/93-1904): a different company, not part of this report.
metadata.freight_only_note: Not drawn (Rule 1): Bloomfield Jct - Blain - New Germantown 1929-1933/35 freight only after the 31 Dec 1928 passenger end; Newport - Bloomfield Jct had no service after 20 Apr 1920.
not_yet_sourced: SR&W takeover year: 31 Mar 1920 (chronology) vs 1921 (Blain marker). Split drawn at 1920.
Newport-end last train: 20 Apr 1920 suspension (chronology) vs 'last train left in 1921' (blog) and 'ceased business in 1921' (Newport marker, read as abandonment).
1891 passenger use Newport - Loysville (section opened 1891): not confirmed; drawn from 1892.
New Germantown 1920-28: no source names it; the 1928 end is the line-wide Blain-marker date. No evidence of an earlier cutback to Blain, but none against it.
Nature of 1920-28 service (mixed vs passenger; through cars to New Bloomfield / Duncannon): not found.
Headway: 'twice a day' (Blain marker) is undated; avg_speed_kmh is unsourced.
Mileage: Fowler 29.1 mi Newport - New Germantown vs Wikipedia 30.67 mi, not reconciled.

Primary sources still wanted: Kohler & Weinshencker's book, the marker texts (hmdb.org returned 403), PA Secretary of Internal Affairs railroad reports, Perry County Times / Duncannon Record around 31 Dec 1928.
Newport terminal position is an estimate beside the PRR station; Bloomfield Junction is placed at the OHM grade crossing.

properties.line: Newport and Sherman's Valley: Newport – Blain
properties.speed_source: estimated: 3 ft gauge steam, mixed passenger/freight trains on a winding valley line; no timetable with running times was read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-21): untagged railway=abandoned ways named 'Newport & Shermans Valley' / 'Newport and Shermans Valley Railroad' (no old_railway_operator or note:old_railway_operator on any of them); OpenHistoricalMap (overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org, 2026-10-21): unnamed railway=rail ways -205160806 and -205198671 (OHM ids 205160806, 205198671; start_date 1890, end_date 1935). Assembled way-by-way in order with opstrace.py helpers (douglas_peucker 8 m, trim_reversals); gaps bridged straight.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 24.42 mi against 25.4 mi documented (Fowler: Newport - Bloomfield Jn 8.3 + Bloomfield Jn - Blain 17.1; -3.9%). Newport - Bloomfield Junction 8.29 mi vs 8.3; Bloomfield Junction - Blain 16.13 mi vs 17.1 (-5.7%; Elliottsburg - Loysville draws about 3.5 mi against Fowler's 4.1). Bloomfield Junction - Blain (16.1 mi) is fully traced along the OHM N&SV grade ways -205160806 and -205198671, dated 1890-1935, i.e. the line's own alignment; OSM way 580263656 (Loysville - Blain, 'Newport and Shermans Valley Railroad') agrees with it within 22 m. Bloomfield Junction is placed where the OHM N&SV grade (-205160806) crosses OHM's Perry County Railroad grade (-205198668) at 40.4044,-77.2324, 2.29 mi west of New Bloomfield (Fowler: 2.5 mi of track). Newport - Bloomfield Junction is traced on the OSM-mapped grade (ways 1360650883, 1360650882, 1360650881, 1360650880, 1360650885, 1360650886, 1032421985, then the first 0.70 mi of OHM -205160806) with gaps: STRAIGHT LINES on Newport - Bloomfield Junction, 3.78 mi in all, where OSM's mapped grade is broken: (a) 0.96 mi from the Newport terminal (a hand-pinned estimate beside the PRR station; the N&SV terminus position is not surveyed) to the east end of OSM way 1360650883 near the mouth of Little Buffalo Creek; (b) 0.45 mi, way 1360650883 to 1360650882; (c) 0.46 mi, 1360650882 to 1360650881; (d) 0.90 mi, 1360650881 to 1360650880 (these three bridge the grade through Little Buffalo State Park around Juniata Furnace/Wahneta); (e) 0.31 mi, 1360650885 to 1360650886; (f) 0.33 mi, 1360650886 to 1032421985; (g) 0.37 mi, south end of 1032421985 to the NE end of OHM way -205160806; plus a 23 m link 1360650880-1360650885. No later alignment is drawn: the line was never rebuilt; the traced ways are its own (lifted 1921 at the Newport end, 1933-35 elsewhere). Waypoint fit: Juniata Furnace 0.3 km, Wahneta 0.5 km, Elliottsburg 0.1 km, Loysville 0.1 km, Andersonburg 0.3 km, Blain 0.2 km from the line. Green Park: the hamlet's Nominatim point sits on OHM's Perry County RR Landisburg extension (1893-1904), not on the N&SV, which passes about 0.2 km north.

segments.note: Newport (PRR Main Line) - Juniata Furnace - Wahneta - Sylvan - McKee - Bloomfield Junction (Tressler) - Elliottsburg - Green Park - Loysville - Fort Robinson - Center - Cisna Run - Andersonburg - Blain, 3 ft gauge, built by lumberman David Gring; mixed passenger/freight steam trains. Newport - Loysville opened 1891, but no source read says passengers rode before the first train into Blain on 18 Jan 1892, which ran from Newport, so the drawn start is 1892 (the 1893 Official Guide, via Fowler's letter z, lists the stations independently). Ends 1920: on 20 Apr 1920 train service was suspended between Newport and New Bloomfield Junction, and the Public Service Commission dismissed Newport's complaint on 9 Nov 1920 because the narrow-gauge company no longer existed; the Newport end was abandoned and lifted in 1921. Source conflict: the Newport 'Railroad Era' marker says the road 'ceased business in 1921' and a blog post says the last train 'left in 1921' - read here as the abandonment, not the passenger end. Bloomfield Junction - Blain continued after 1920 under the Susquehanna River and Western (separate feature). Ownership-change date conflict: the chronology (pvrr.blogspot, after Kohler & Weinshencker) gives the sale of the N&SV with the SR&W to Rodney Gring and George H. Ross on 31 Mar 1920 and its absorption into the SR&W; the 2020 Blain marker dates the SR&W takeover 1921. This layer splits at 1920, the dated sale. Under USRA federal control 28 Dec 1917 - 29 Jun 1918 (not an operator change). headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the Blain marker's undated 'twice a day' passenger and freight trains to and from Blain 'for almost 30 years' (two round trips a day), not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1892 start from the Blain marker (first train into Blain 18 Jan 1892, via search summary only) and the 1893 Official Guide via Fowler table 427/457 letter z; 1920 end from the Kohler & Weinshencker chronology (20 Apr 1920 Newport suspension, 31 Mar 1920 sale, Nov 1920 PSC dismissal). Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 3.88 mi against 3.7 mi documented (Fowler SR&W MPs 30.7-34.4; 4.9%). Traced on OHM -205198671's last metres at Blain and OSM ways 1202318771 and 1202318769 ('Newport and Shermans Valley Railroad') into New Germantown; ends at the point of 1202318769 nearest the New Germantown station site (40.3073,-77.5704; 0.1 km from the hand-pinned station). STRAIGHT LINES on Blain - New Germantown, 2.63 mi in all: 0.15 mi from the end of the OHM grade at Blain to OSM way 1202318771, and 2.48 mi from 1202318771 (west edge of Blain) to the east end of OSM way 1202318769 (east of New Germantown), through Clark's Run and Mount Pleasant, where neither OSM nor OHM has the grade; PA 274 runs alongside in the same valley but was not used as a substitute. Way 1202318769 continues west past the station onto the abortive Path Valley / Perry Lumber grade (1360642536, 1043832900); that part is NOT drawn (never a passenger line).

segments.note: Blain - Clark's Run - Mount Pleasant - New Germantown, the 1893 extension (chronology: 'The N&SVRR completes its line to New Germantown', 1893; all three stations carry Fowler's z = 1893 Official Guide). Ends 1920 with the N&SV's absorption into the Susquehanna River and Western; continued under the SR&W to 1928 (separate feature). Ownership-change date conflict: the chronology (pvrr.blogspot, after Kohler & Weinshencker) gives the sale of the N&SV with the SR&W to Rodney Gring and George H. Ross on 31 Mar 1920 and its absorption into the SR&W; the 2020 Blain marker dates the SR&W takeover 1921. This layer splits at 1920, the dated sale. New Germantown was the jumping-off point for the abortive 1893-94 Path Valley extension, never completed and not drawn. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the Blain marker's undated 'twice a day' passenger and freight trains to and from Blain 'for almost 30 years' (two round trips a day), not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1893 start from the pvrr.blogspot chronology and Fowler table 457 letter z (1893 Official Guide) at Clark's Run, Mount Pleasant and New Germantown; 1920 end from the dated 31 Mar 1920 sale in the same chronology. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

Bloomfield Junction is placed where the OHM N&SV grade (-205160806) crosses OHM's Perry County Railroad grade (-205198668) at 40.4044,-77.2324, 2.29 mi west of New Bloomfield (Fowler: 2.5 mi of track). STRAIGHT LINES on Blain - New Germantown, 2.63 mi in all: 0.15 mi from the end of the OHM grade at Blain to OSM way 1202318771, and 2.48 mi from 1202318771 (west edge of Blain) to the east end of OSM way 1202318769 (east of New Germantown), through Clark's Run and Mount Pleasant, where neither OSM nor OHM has the grade; PA 274 runs alongside in the same valley but was not used as a substitute. segments.note: Bloomfield Junction - Elliottsburg - Loysville - Andersonburg - Blain - New Germantown under the Susquehanna River and Western after the N&SV's absorption on 31 Mar 1920; with the Newport end closed (20 Apr 1920) the narrow gauge's outlet was via the dual-gauge New Bloomfield connection and the SR&W to Duncannon (the connection itself is not drawn here - no source says narrow-gauge passenger trains ran into New Bloomfield). Ownership-change date conflict: the chronology (pvrr.blogspot, after Kohler & Weinshencker) gives the sale of the N&SV with the SR&W to Rodney Gring and George H. Ross on 31 Mar 1920 and its absorption into the SR&W; the 2020 Blain marker dates the SR&W takeover 1921. This layer splits at 1920, the dated sale. Ends 31 Dec 1928, when the SR&W ended passenger runs (Blain marker, corroborated by Gilmore 2017 via pahistoricpreservation.com: 'The Blain train station ended passenger service in 1928'). New Germantown is not named by any source for 1920-28: its 1928 end inherits the line-wide marker date, with no evidence of an earlier cutback either way. Whether the last years were a mixed or a separate passenger train is not known; either counts. Freight continued: Blain - New Germantown and Blain - Loysville abandoned 1933, Loysville - New Bloomfield 1934-35, last rails lifted April 1935 - those freight-only years are not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min is an ESTIMATE carried over from the marker's undated 'twice a day'; no SR&W timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: 1920 start from the 31 Mar 1920 sale in the pvrr.blogspot chronology (Blain marker says 1921 - conflict recorded in note); 1928 end from the Blain marker (via search summary only; hmdb.org returned 403) and Gilmore 2017 cited by pahistoricpreservation.com. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
